title: Elemental Analysis of the Analytes Desorbed from Escherichia coli DH5α Cells with Different Wash Buffer for Zeta Potential Analysis
content: Measurement of bacterial cell surface charge via zeta potential dynamic light scattering is a popular method. In this approach, the bacterial cell is moved via an applied electric field, and its speed of movement provides an estimate of its cell surface charge. Hence, the types of biomolecules and inorganic ions on the bacterial cell surface deeply influence this measurement, and they must be removed via multiple washes of wash buffer of appropriate ionic strength. In this work, an attempt was made to use inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to measure the ionic composition of the wash buffer to help understand the types and concentrations of ions that are removed from the Escherichia coli cell surface during different washes of its surface by different wash buffer of differing ionic strength. Data obtained revealed that there were substantial removal of magnesium (up to 14 ppm) and calcium (up to 15 to 20 ppm in the first wash of the E. coli cell surface by different wash buffer. In subsequent wash 2 and 3, there was much less removal of different ionic elements, with maximal removal at about 0.15 to 0.20 ppm. Hence, it is likely that divalent magnesium and calcium played important roles in stabilizing the nonspecifically adsorbed biomolecules on the E. coli cell surface.
